answer: The timber multiplier is published, charged in ember, and inlet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 816 identities would post 2674 proofs and burn roughly 56 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
